A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSTP work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables that can be matched reliably. The supplied v2 ends with references; v3 includes Appendix A, which was also inspected.

before.justification: v2 reports original subset-training experiments on Argoverse 1 and 2, including prediction accuracy, component ablations, sensitivity studies and training times.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and reports additional comparisons, density-stratified evaluations and low-retention experiments in its main text and appendix.

M1.justification: Density partitioning, gradient extraction, cosine-based selection scores and descending-density budget allocation remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 renames DynamicBudget to DynamicSelect without changing its steps; the new biased-sampling terminology describes the existing allocation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate trajectory forecasting on Argoverse 1 and Argoverse 2 with the same observation and prediction horizons. Additional density illustrations, model evaluations and retention budgets remain within this existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds augmentation, reweighting, epoch-wise reselection and High-density+Random comparisons. It also adds Herding to the Argoverse 2 comparison and Cluster/Herding to the existing density-stratified comparison. These substantially expand the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: The core metrics, six predicted modes and benchmark protocols are retained. v3 adds 5%, 2% and 1% retention settings, differently sized controls in Table 1, and changes the efficiency example from 50% to 60% retention. Appendix A.1 mainly discloses existing training settings rather than establishing that they changed.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of alternative balancing strategies, extreme data-budget degradation and detailed HPNet performance across density strata, while extending backbone sensitivity results across retention ratios. The existing component, pretraining-epoch and partition-interval ablations are retained, with the latter two moved to Appendix A.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experiments. Both present point estimates; varying pretraining epochs is a sensitivity experiment rather than repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial result entries for new comparators, HPNet density evaluations, smaller subsets and backbone transfers. Existing values also change: Table 2's HiVT-64 SSTP result at 50% retention changes from 0.704/1.073/0.111 to 0.706/1.074/0.110 for minADE/minFDE/MR. Revised timing results use a different retention setting and therefore do not establish a same-setting efficiency change.

T1.justification: v3 Section 2 introduces a formal (1 - 1/e) approximation guarantee in Equation 7 and an O(|D|d) + O(Bd) computational-complexity claim, neither present in v2. These are substantive theoretical additions, although no supporting proof or conditions establishing the guarantee are supplied.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that SSTP constructs compact, balanced trajectory datasets, preserves accuracy using roughly half the data, improves high-density prediction, reduces training cost and transfers across architectures. v3 foregrounds density imbalance and reorganizes the contribution bullets without materially changing these central claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving gradient domination and under-training of shared attention parameters, asserts asymmetric transfer from complex to simpler scenes, and interprets why naive balancing alternatives fail. It also explicitly limits demonstrated applicability to Argoverse trajectory prediction and discusses the observed degradation at extremely low retention.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 substantially expands reproducibility details through selection batch sizes, optimizers, learning rates, schedules, architecture settings and augmentations for the existing predictors. Conversely, v3 removes the RTX 4090 disclosure and explicit repository URL; its reproducibility statement mentions code and checkpoints through an unspecified anonymous link.

R1.justification: The literature coverage and positioning against trajectory prediction, long-tail learning and sample-selection work remain largely unchanged. v3 removes Chen et al.'s Super-samples from kernel herding reference, previously cited in v2 Table 2; the citation-style conversion and related-work relocation are presentation changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method narrative are substantially rewritten. Related work moves after experiments, the experimental narrative is reorganized, and several analyses move into a structured appendix. Ethics, reproducibility and LLM-usage statements are also added.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. Figure 1 is redesigned, timing becomes a separate figure, scene examples and density histograms are separated, and the retention plot drops its minFDE panels. v3 also adds comparison tables and appendix scene grids while relocating existing ablation tables.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical scrutiny through alternative-strategy comparisons and extreme-budget tests, and Appendix A.1 improves implementation disclosure. However, it introduces an unsupported approximation guarantee, removes the explicit code URL, and claims over 50% time reduction in Figure 5 despite reporting 7.25 versus 7.78 hours for HiVT and about 45% reduction for HPNet. These gains in evidence and documentation coexist with material losses in rigor and access information, leaving the net quality direction unclear.
